summary: Core scavenged materials and fasteners required for primitive crafting.

items.description: A respectable length of wood, just big enough to wrap your hand around.  Makes a decent melee weapon.
uses: Source: smash bushes or furniture; base handle for primitive tools.

items.description: A straight section of wood, about eight feet long and a couple of inches in diameter.  Makes a decent melee weapon, and can be broken into shorter pieces for crafting.
uses: Harvest from small trees; carve into spears or tool hafts.

items.description: A stout pole with one end sharpened to a point.
uses: Fire-harden to upgrade into wooden spears quickly.

items.description: A flat, thick plank of wood, like a 2 by 4 or similar piece of dimensional lumber.  Makes a decent melee weapon if you're desperate, and can be used for all kinds of construction projects.
uses: Salvage from furniture; essential for construction and tool handles.

items.description: A rock the size of a baseball.  Makes a decent melee weapon, and is also good for throwing at enemies.
uses: Gather from ground; combine with sticks for basic stone tools.

items.description: A baseball-sized rock with a somewhat sharp edge that also chips in a semi-predictable way if struck.  With the right skills, you could give it a better edge.
uses: Knapped from rocks; substitute for simple cutting edges.

items.description: A rock the size of a baseball which chips in a semi-predictable way if struck, leaving a sharp edge.  Makes a decent melee weapon, and is also good for throwing at enemies.
uses: Abstract requirement satisfied by flint/sharp rocks for knapping.

items.description: A chunk of flint, the kind of rock that can make sparks if stuck against high-carbon steel.  It also chips in a semi-predictable way if struck, leaving a sharp edge.
uses: Superior knapping stone; boosts success crafting stone blades.

items.description: A splintered piece of wood, could be used as a skewer or for kindling.
uses: Byproduct of smashing furniture; used in fire drill crafting.

items.description: A steel pipe; makes a good melee weapon.  Useful in a bunch of crafting recipes.
uses: Smash lockers or disassemble furniture to harvest metal piping.

items.description: A pin-shaped piece of iron.  It can be used to construct various things with a hammer.
uses: Recovered from smashed furniture; fasteners for primitive shovel.

items.description: A hardwood stick designed for hitting colorful balls around a felt table.  Truly, the coolest of sports.
uses: Loot from bars; substitute shaft for cudgel crafting.

items.description: A roll of incredibly strong tape.  Its uses are innumerable.
uses: Multi-purpose adhesive; holds primitive shovel blade securely.

items.description: Tough, thin fiber taken from a plant.  Can be used as thread.
uses: Collect by butchering vegetation; twist into cordage.

items.description: A 6-inch (or about 15 cm) long piece of natural cordage.  Useful for some purposes, but not as strong or flexible as proper string.
uses: Craft from plant fibre; six-inch segment for lashing tools.

items.description: A 6-inch (or about 15 cm) long piece of leather lace.  Useful for some purposes, but not as flexible as proper string.
uses: Use leather straps when plant fibre unavailable.

items.description: A 6-inch (or about 15 cm) long piece of cotton string.
uses: Cut from longer string; alternative lashing for stone tools.

items.description: A tough sinew cut from a corpse, usable as thread.
uses: Harvest from butchered corpses; strong natural cordage.

items.description: A length of wool yarn that could be used to knit wool clothing.
uses: Unravel sweaters for emergency cordage.

items.description: A small quantity of thread that could be used for sewing.
uses: Harvest from clothing; universal crafting input.

items.description: Some tough canvas-weight thread, sturdier than ordinary thread.  You could meticulously weave this into a sheet of canvas cloth.  It would also be useful for stitching such sheets together, though it's fine to use for normal tailoring projects too.
uses: Salvaged from heavy-duty gear; tougher than cotton thread.

items.description: Heat-resistant Nomex thread that would be particularly useful for making heat protection gear, though it's fine to use in place of normal thread too, in most cases.
uses: Fireproof thread recovered from firefighter gear.

items.description: Very durable Kevlar thread that would be particularly useful for making ballistic armor, though it's fine to use in place of normal thread too, in most cases.  Making armor-grade Kevlar sheets from this would need a particularly tight weave, and so would require some specialized machinery.
uses: High-tension thread; useful for durable tool lashings.

items.description: A handful of New England sand.  If you had a stoked furnace, you could turn it into glass.  Otherwise, it's only good for making cement.
uses: Shovel from river banks; used for grinding stone edges.

items.description: A handful of gravel, smaller than pebbles but larger than sand.
uses: Collect from construction sites; abrasive for stone tools.

items.description: A solution of sterilized water and salt for intravenous infusion or washing contaminants from one's eyes.
uses: Medical supply; used as coolant/grinding medium in recipes.
Charges per stack: 5

items.description: A 72 by 24 inch two-layer-thick fabric sheet.  It could be used as a curtain or bedsheet, or cut up for a bunch of smaller sheets.
uses: Rip from beds; required for makeshift sling crafting.

items.description: seeing this is a bug
uses: Requires campfire or brazier; treat as ever-present heat source.

items.description: Generic requirement representing 10 inches of thread, sinew, fiber, canvas, or yarn.
uses: Satisfies crafting requirements calling for sewing-capable filament.
